statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is the minimum number of moves needed to delete all elements of arr. A move is defined as follows: from a current sequence s, choose indices i,j with 0 <= i <= j < len(s) such that s[i],...,s[j] is a palindrome, meaning that for every t with 0 <= t <= j-i, s[i+t] = s[j-t]; replace s by the concatenation of s[0..i-1] and s[j+1..len(s)-1]. A complete deletion is a finite sequence of such replacements starting at arr and ending at the empty sequence; r is the least number of moves among all complete deletions of arr.
preconditions: arr is a slice of i64 with 1 <= len(arr) <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 20.

statement: For every arr satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r: it does not fail because of arithmetic overflow, out-of-bounds indexing, or panic.
preconditions: arr is a slice of i64 with 1 <= len(arr) <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 20.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 1 <= r <= len(arr).
preconditions: arr is a slice of i64 with 1 <= len(arr) <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 20.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, let odd_count be the number of values v with 1 <= v <= 20 for which the count of indices i satisfying 0 <= i < len(arr) and arr[i] = v is odd. Then r >= odd_count.
preconditions: arr is a slice of i64 with 1 <= len(arr) <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 20.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 1 if and only if arr is a palindrome, meaning that for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), arr[i] = arr[len(arr)-1-i].
preconditions: arr is a slice of i64 with 1 <= len(arr) <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 20.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 1 if arr[0] = arr[1], and r = 2 otherwise.
preconditions: arr is a slice of i64 with len(arr) = 2, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 20.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 1 if arr[0] = arr[2]; otherwise r = 2 if arr[0] = arr[1] or arr[1] = arr[2]; otherwise r = 3.
preconditions: arr is a slice of i64 with len(arr) = 3, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 20.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = len(arr).
preconditions: arr is a slice of i64 with 1 <= len(arr) <= 100, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 20, and for every i,j with 0 <= i < j < len(arr), arr[i] != arr[j].

statement: Let rev(arr) be the slice of length len(arr) with rev(arr)[i] = arr[len(arr)-1-i] for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr). If minimum_moves(arr) = Ok r, then minimum_moves(rev(arr)) = Ok r.
preconditions: arr is a slice of i64 with 1 <= len(arr) <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 20.

statement: If minimum_moves(arr) = Ok r, then minimum_moves(arr2) = Ok (r+1).
preconditions: arr is a slice of i64 with 1 <= len(arr) <= 99, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 20, x is an i64 with 1 <= x <= 20, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), arr[i] != x. Let arr2 be the slice obtained by appending x to arr, so len(arr2) = len(arr)+1 and arr2[len(arr)] = x.

statement: If minimum_moves(arr) = Ok r and minimum_moves(arr2) = Ok r2, then r2 <= r+1.
preconditions: arr is a slice of i64 with 1 <= len(arr) <= 99, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 20. Also x is an i64 with 1 <= x <= 20, p is an integer with 0 <= p <= len(arr), and arr2 is the slice obtained by inserting x at position p in arr.

statement: Whenever minimum_moves(arr) = Ok r, minimum_moves(L) = Ok rL, and minimum_moves(R) = Ok rR, it holds that r <= rL + rR.
preconditions: arr is a slice of i64 with 2 <= len(arr) <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 20. For an integer k with 0 <= k < len(arr)-1, let L = arr[0..k] and R = arr[k+1..len(arr)-1].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r > 1, there exist indices i,j with 0 <= i <= j < len(arr) such that arr[i],...,arr[j] is a palindrome, it is not the case that i = 0 and j = len(arr)-1, and if arr' is obtained from arr by deleting positions i through j and concatenating the remaining prefix and suffix, then minimum_moves(arr') = Ok (r-1).
preconditions: arr is a slice of i64 with 1 <= len(arr) <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 20.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = 2.
preconditions: arr is a slice of i64 with 2 <= len(arr) <= 100, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 20, arr is not a palindrome, and there exists k with 0 <= k < len(arr)-1 such that both L = arr[0..k] and R = arr[k+1..len(arr)-1] are palindromes.

statement: If minimum_moves(arr) = Ok r and minimum_moves(arr2) = Ok r2, then r <= r2 <= r+1.
preconditions: arr is a slice of i64 with 1 <= len(arr) <= 99, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 20. Also x is an i64 with 1 <= x <= 20, x does not occur in arr, p is an integer with 0 <= p <= len(arr), and arr2 is the slice obtained by inserting x at position p in arr, so len(arr2)=len(arr)+1 and arr2[p]=x.
